findings.text: Ask 4 is not done: no `log` line lists tonight's misfiled children (agent id, current parent_session) anywhere. The `children-link` task in `cloud-voice-app-20261106/session.jsonl` holds only voice-app's own root-cause log (line 539), and this folder's `session.jsonl` has no log at all. Fix: list the registry rows whose `parent_session` is `voice-20261019-live-page` with a script and append them as one log line on that task.

A fresh agent could not continue from this folder alone. `session.jsonl` holds only the assign, the pid and commit `a3f5c0d04`: there is no record that `RemoteMCP.test.mjs` passed, that asks 1–3 are met, or that ask 4 is still open. Log each step's outcome on the task. (I ran the test in the worktree: `ok 7 calls`, exit 0.)

The test copies the parent rule instead of calling it (`RemoteMCP.test.mjs`, the block added around line 172): `session_of` and the `child.parent_session` assignment are written out again because importing Agents needs the SDK. So a later change to `Agents.register` or `session_of` (`Agents.js:66`, `:92`) would not fail this test. The comment explains why, and that is acceptable for a lean test.

The brief says "live and registry". `voice-app` is never in `agents.live`: only `Agents.js:276`, `Dispatcher.js` and `Sessions.js` put agents there. So `session_of` falls through to the registry row, and writing only the registry is enough. One clause in `voice-logging.md` saying so would stop the next reader from looking for a live entry.

`point_caller` (`RemoteMCP.js:215`) runs on every voice tool call and reads `registry.json` each time. It writes only when the id changes, so this is cheap and correct. `External.register` also bumps `last_at`, which the brief's "nothing else changes" tolerates.
